decision: Replace OpenClaw with Nous Research Hermes Agent
why: The OpenClaw scaffold never installed anything. Hermes has a documented OpenClaw import path, explicit approvals and deny rules, per-platform toolsets, and a Docker execution backend, so it fits the read-only pilot better.

decision: Run a read-only pilot before any execution
why: Web search and an in-memory task list answer the health-summary use case without host access.
No messaging platform, gateway service, listening port, or bot token is needed for Phase 1.

decision: Disable toolsets globally, not only per platform
why: A per-platform row can be changed later. `agent.disabled_toolsets` is applied after platform configuration, so it cannot be re-enabled by accident.

decision: Use a TypeScript validator run by Bun
why: The repository is Bun-only per the core standard; Bun ships a YAML parser, so the validator needs no runtime dependency.

decision: Allow only Docker if execution is widened
why: The local terminal backend has no isolation. The Docker backend can run with no network, no host mounts, no forwarded secrets, and no extra flags.

decision: Keep model, provider, and owner values as placeholders in Git
why: Phase 0 chooses them, and the validator rejects a concrete value in the template.

decision: Run oxlint directly instead of `bun lint --no-script`
why: Bun 1.4.5 has no `bun lint` subcommand and returns `Script not found "lint"`. The pinned oxlint binary from mise is the same linter the core standard names.
